hikes.name: Canyon Overlook Trail
highlights: Short, easy path with sweeping views of Zion Canyon, the Towers of the Virgin, and the Great Arch.
Passes through a shaded grotto and over slickrock before reaching the cliff-edge overlook.
Requires a private vehicle -- the shuttle doesn't stop at this trailhead.

hikes.name: The Narrows: Riverside Walk
highlights: Paved, wheelchair-accessible path along the Virgin River to the mouth of Zion's famous slot canyon.
Ends at a sandy beach where hikers can wade in before continuing (unmaintained) into The Narrows proper.
Reachable only by shuttle during peak season (Feb-Nov).

hikes.name: Emerald Pools Trail
highlights: Loop past three pools and seasonal waterfalls, starting at Zion Lodge.
Family-friendly and heavily trafficked; rocky sections near the Upper Pool are a common source of minor injuries.

hikes.name: Angels Landing Trail
hikes.difficulty_override_reason: Distance/elevation alone compute to Moderate, but the final half-mile is a chain-assisted Class 3 scramble with major fall exposure on both sides -- NPS itself rates this Strenuous. Textbook manual-override case per docs/spec.md §3.2.1.
highlights: Zion's most iconic and most popular hike -- the final half-mile follows a chain-assisted spine with steep exposure on both sides.
Requires an advance lottery permit to hike past Scout Lookout.
Includes Walter's Wiggles, 21 switchbacks named for Zion's first superintendent.

hikes.name: Observation Point via Stave Spring Trailhead
highlights: The current route to Observation Point since the classic East Rim approach closed after a 2019 rockfall.
Long, quiet, high-desert hike ending about 700 ft above Angels Landing itself.
Requires a rough access road; many 2WD vehicles park a quarter-mile short of the trailhead.
